question: How did killer whales in the Aleutian Islands end up wiping out underwater kelp forests?
answer: By eating sea otters. In the 1990s some killer whales, perhaps short of seals, turned to otters, whose numbers crashed. Otters eat sea urchins; freed of them, the urchins multiplied and grazed the kelp down to bare rock. Estes and colleagues traced the whole chain, four links from an open-ocean hunter to a vanished forest.
move: Trace a change at least three links before declaring it harmless.
ask: Whose small change might ripple, three steps on, into my own life?
reference: Estes, Tinker, Williams & Doak, Killer whale predation on sea otters linking oceanic and nearshore ecosystems, Science, 1998
